response.consequence: On Linux, re-running the script when .env already has GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL leaves the stale URL in place. The script still prints "✅ Updated". A failed run also exits with status 0.
response.explanation: The script updates an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with `sed -i '' -E ...`. That form works only with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU sed (Linux), the empty string is read as the script and the real expression is treated as a file name, so the replacement fails and the existing .env line is not updated. Separately, the failure paths (no tunnel URL, rate limit) call `cleanup`, which always runs `exit 0`, so callers can't tell that the script failed.

Those columns are only refreshed by the users trigger, which fires on changes to the user row, and by the full refresh function. When a booking is reassigned to another host, the denormalized row therefore holds the new user id with the old user's name, email and avatar. Two related gaps exist. The booking INSERT trigger reuses this function and updates WHERE rfrd."bookingId" = NEW.id. A response written before its booking exists has a NULL bookingId, so no row matches and it is never linked to the booking. The function also never refreshes the assignment reason or the tracking (utm) columns.
